q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a steel cot?
title: Steel cot carbon footprint per cot
short: Weigh the steel tubes, sheet and fittings per cot and multiply by the steel supplier's figure. Add cutting, bending, welding and powder coating energy, then divide the workshop's energy by cots made.

ul: Steel sheet or slats for the base.

p: Report per cot by size and weight. Steel is usually most of the footprint, so weight is the main driver.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per cot (one month)
lines: Plant total: 12,620 / 1,200 = 10.5 kg CO2 per cot
Add steel and powder for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
